thread:
amy: heads-up — hit a nasty combo of issues w/ python async client today when our webhook consumer retried a streaming generate. duplicates + loop stalls :grimacing:

amy: minimal repro: we call client.chat.stream(...) inside an aiohttp handler, transient 5xx -> sdk retries -> we get the same output twice and the event loop freezes for ~2s.

amy: gist of code:
```py
# inside aiohttp handler
async def handler(req):
    async with client.stream("chat.completions", model="r-test") as stream:
        async for chunk in stream:
            await ws.send_str(chunk.text)
```

amy: observed logs show retry backoff uses time.sleep (blocking) in async path and the replay doesn't attach idempotency-key for streaming requests so the server re-executes partial side-effects.

jordan: ack — thanks for the clear repro. that blocking sleep in the async adapter was a poor oversight. can you paste the exact logs/stack?

amy: pasted stack snippet:
```
File ".../redwood_sdk/transport/async_retry.py", line 47, in _do_retry
    time.sleep(backoff)  # <- blocking
```

amy: and server logs show two separate requests w/ no idempotency header for streaming path, so server can't dedupe.

kai: interesting. on the runtime side we rely on idempotency tokens for create-like endpoints. streaming endpoints historically bypassed body-preservation because bodies were consumed as iterator.

samir: two separate problems: (1) blocking sleep in async retry; (2) no preserved idempotency token / inability to re-send stream body on replay. both need different solutions.

jordan: proposed fixes:
- replace time.sleep with asyncio.sleep in async transport (low effort)
- add 'max_inflight' and 'retry_strategy' config UX so teams can opt into safe replay for streaming endpoints
- for streaming bodies, implement automatic buffering up to configurable limit (e.g., 64KB) and fail-light when body too large with explicit error message

amy: buffering makes sense as fallback. for our webhook consumer the streaming payloads are small so a short buffer would solve. downside is memory for large streams — need clear docs + opt-in.

kai: runtime-side, we can add a server-side marker that accepts idempotency for streaming by returning a 409 if duplicate attempt found. but client must include token on initial try — so client change mandatory.

jordan: open question: should streaming endpoints be non-retriable by default? that prevents accidental double-creates but hurts reliability for transient network blips. maybe default to no-retry, but provide an 'enable_stream_replay' flag that does automatic buffering + idempotency header.

samir: agree. also add clear telemetry: when replay triggered for streaming, increment a metric so customers know it's happening.

amy: filed quick bug with repro + logs: https://internal.issue/RED-4567 (cc @jordan @kai)

jordan: i'll take the async sleep -> asyncio.sleep patch and add unit tests. will also sketch a config flag API:
```py
Client(..., retry_config=RetryConfig(type="exponential", max_attempts=3, async_sleep=True, stream_replay=False, stream_buffer_size=65536))
```

jordan: one more: update docs/quickstart to mention that streaming retries are opt-in and show example with small buffer.

kai: i'll coordinate runtime changes (409 on duplicate) and add a short compatibility note for older runtimes that don't support stream idempotency.

amy: reduced repro test added to our integration tests — will push after jordan's patch. thanks :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: release 0.12.4-rc deployed to dev with async-sleep fix by @jordan :rocket:
